goal: A worktree worker run binds a git-based progress probe to each task's sandbox and threads the configured [worker] checkpoint_nudge_seconds from flywheel.toml through orchestrate into the harness, so an iteration nearing its deadline on a branch with no new commits receives the checkpoint nudge in production runs.

relevant: packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- the _git helper and run_once's orchestrate threading; build the per-sandbox git progress-probe factory here (an opaque HEAD-revision token) and pass it through

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_orchestrate.py -- orchestrate/_drive_under_lease already bind per-run closures over the sandbox (landability_gate, ~3148); bind the probe the same way and thread checkpoint_nudge_seconds into run_task_object
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_policy.py -- [worker] parsing (_optional_worker, ~576) is the pattern for the new key
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_sandbox_limit_threading.py -- the committed policy->orchestrate->run threading test pattern to mirror
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_policy.py and packages/flywheel-worktree/tests/test_worker.py -- add the key and probe tests here
docs/configuration.md -- document the new key under the existing [worker] table
constraints: Git awareness lives ONLY in flywheel-worktree: the orchestrator and core handle the probe as an opaque closure (the landability-probe discipline, spec 00061); do NOT change the SubmitStrategy protocol to carry it.
Probe semantics: the opaque token changes iff the sandbox branch gains a new commit (HEAD moves); a raising probe is contained -- it never unwinds the run, and the nudge is simply skipped.
[worker] checkpoint_nudge_seconds: float seconds, default 300.0 when the key or table is absent (default-on -- the retro loss came from this behavior not existing); 0 disables the nudge.
Wire the probe for the worktree backend only; a container-backend run gets no probe this task (nudge dormant there).
Consume the seam checkpoint-nudge-injection defined (the HarnessConfig knob and probe parameter); do not fork a second threshold or probe definition.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not re-implement or alter the core nudge behavior (timing, at-most-once, deadline immobility) -- the prerequisite owns it and its tests must pass unmodified.
Do not place the config key in a [deadlines] table -- phase 14-attempt-budget-config owns that table (see notes).
No container-backend probe, no CLI flag override this task.
Do not modify or weaken existing tests; add new tests only.
edge_cases: A fresh worktree with zero commits past base -> token stable -> nudge-eligible.
After a commit lands in the sandbox -> token changes -> no nudge.
Absent [worker] table -> 300.0 resolves; checkpoint_nudge_seconds = 0 in toml -> the disabled value is what reaches the harness (assert via the threading test, not by running an agent).
Git failure inside the probe (e.g. deleted worktree) -> contained, no nudge, run unaffected.
The probe factory binds per-run: two concurrent pool members' probes must not observe each other's sandboxes.
context.notes: FLAG (shared invariant, cross-phase, no edge declared): phase 14-attempt-budget-config concurrently adds a top-level [deadlines] table to _policy.py/docs/configuration.md. This key deliberately lives under [worker] so the overlap is textual-merge-only. The semantic composition point is already handled: the prerequisite computes remaining time against the RESOLVED AGENT_ITERATION ceiling (config.deadlines.for_class), so phase 14's operator overrides flow into the nudge with no coordination.
